answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a pearl-like escrow: each agent locks a small time-locked deposit before joining, a lantern held up to reveal who is real. Value accrues only through completed honest epochs, each releasing part of the refund, so a fake must endure the same long terrace of waiting periods and do real work before its bond returns. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must lock capital per identity for the whole epoch while earning nothing and loses deposits via slashing, so forgery costs more than honesty.
